original_query: SELECT * FROM (SELECT DEPT.DEPTNO, DEPT.NAME FROM DEPT INNER JOIN (SELECT DEPTNO FROM EMP GROUP BY DEPTNO) AS t0 ON DEPT.DEPTNO = t0.DEPTNO) AS t1 WHERE t1.DEPTNO <= 10
rewritten_query:
SELECT d.deptno,
       d.name
FROM dept AS d
WHERE d.deptno <= 10
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM emp AS e
      WHERE e.deptno = d.deptno
  );

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the derived table `SELECT DEPTNO FROM EMP GROUP BY DEPTNO` with an `EXISTS` semi-join. This eliminates the full aggregation over 45M EMP rows and allows the optimizer to stop at the first matching EMP row per DEPT.
Push the predicate `DEPTNO <= 10` directly onto the DEPT table scan instead of applying it after the join in the outer wrapper, reducing the outer side before the semi-join.
Remove the unnecessary outer `SELECT * FROM (...)` wrapper and the redundant derived table aliases; select only the needed columns directly.
An index on EMP(DEPTNO) is recommended (`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_emp_deptno ON emp (deptno);`) so the EXISTS check becomes at most ~10 index probes instead of scanning and grouping 45M rows.
